citation.title: Adversarial Agents on Topology Optimization: Understanding the Fragility and Robustness of Deep Learning-based and Physics-Based Design Models under Adversarial Perturbation
citation.authors: Hoang Anh Nguyen, Yuan Hong, Hongyi Xu

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Classical SIMP largely restores compliance after adversarial initializations that severely degrade learned surrogate designs; its median rerun-to-reference compliance ratio is 1.000 across tested models.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No measured timing comparison is reported.
claim.alternatives: Abstract qualitatively says SIMP recovers near-reference compliance; Section 5.1 reports clean surrogate/reference compliance ratios, and Section 5.2 reports attacked versus clean surrogate ratios.

baseline.classical_method: SIMP with optimality-criteria updates and sensitivity filtering (Section 2.1)
baseline.implementation: Top88/SIMP mentioned in Section 3 and Appendix A.5; implementation of main reference runs not stated
baseline.data_generation_cost: 300 SIMP target samples; generation time not stated (Section 4)
baseline.quality_metric: Thresholded-design finite-element compliance relative to SIMP reference; IoU, F1, binary accuracy (Sections 3.4, 5.1)
baseline.quality_gap: SIMP rerun median/reference compliance 1.000 across nine models; clean surrogate/reference medians 0.999–1.047 (Sections 5.1, 5.4; Table 3)

R1.evidence: Conclusion and Table 3 compare compliance after attack and rerun; no timed speed comparison is made.

R2.evidence: Sections 5.1–5.4 use SIMP as a quality reference and do not compare runtimes.

R3.evidence: Conclusion makes a mechanical robustness claim, without a measured speed claim.

R4.evidence: Sections 3.4 and 5.2–5.4 evaluate returned designs with finite-element compliance and count severe failures; target volume is specified in Section 4, but realized output volume or volume-constraint violations are not reported.

reporting.n_test_cases: 45 held-out cases per model (Section 4); nine main model configurations (Section 5.4)

notes: Section 4 gives seed-0 split and a common training seed; Section 5.4 counts residual compliance exceedances and Section 4 reports zero dataset solver failures. Data Availability promises data/model upon acceptance and email request, not current public code.
